title: The complement of an invertible ideal is scheme-theoretically dominant
statement: Let Y be a scheme and let C be a quasi-coherent effective Cartier ideal [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal]. The inclusion of the open complement of its support has zero kernel on the structure sheaf, that is, it is scheme-theoretically dominant [def-nagata-scheme-theoretically-dense-open]. No quasi-compactness of Y is assumed.

source.place: Tag 07ZU, Lemma complement-effective-Cartier-divisor, density assertion and proof

proof.text: Use the affine neighborhoods with regular principal generator a supplied by IsInvertible. On each such neighborhood identify the complement of the support with D(a) using the support and zero-locus formulas. Restriction to D(a) is localization away from a, injective by [lem-pc-affine-localization-injective]. Therefore the ideal of the kernel vanishes on each neighborhood. IdealSheafData.ext_of_iSup_eq_top then gives that the kernel ideal sheaf is zero. This is exactly the existing proved source-library theorem IsInvertible.isSchemeTheoreticallyDominant_compl_support.
